title: Streaming Markdown Parser
summary: Parse streamed Markdown chunks into text, inline-code, and fenced-code tokens while preserving delimiter state.

testCases.name: public parses inline code across chunks
public parses fenced code across chunks
hidden backticks inside fence stay literal
hidden unclosed inline code flushes at finish
hidden empty chunks are ignored without losing order
hidden empty stream emits no tokens
hidden unclosed fence preserves literal short backticks
hidden triple priority switches from inline to fenced mode
hidden longer runs consume triples before remaining singles

clarifyingQuestions: Should the parser support full Markdown or only code delimiters?
Should language labels after opening fences be included in fenced content?
How should unclosed inline or fenced code be emitted at end of stream?
followUps: Emit each completed token from `feed()` as soon as its delimiter arrives.
Support escaped backticks and memory limits.
followUpGuide: For incremental `feed()`, keep mode, buffer, and up to two pending backticks on an object. Wait for another character or finish() before treating a short pending run as singles: the next chunk might complete a triple. Empty chunks don't resolve that uncertainty. At finish(), interpret remaining short runs using the current mode and flush the final nonempty token.
For language labels, read through the first newline after an opening fence and store that prefix as metadata. Keep following lines as code content.
For memory limits, stream token callbacks and cap the active buffer size. A renderer can still keep a transcript outside the parser.
complexityAnalysis: - Batch scanner: O(n + c) time, where n is total characters and c is chunk count (even empty chunks are visited). Space is O(n) for the joined input, output, and active character buffer.

- Incremental follow-up: O(n + c) total work with a character-list buffer. A feed can also pay O(k) to join a token accumulated across earlier chunks; O(chunk length) alone doesn't describe that call. Space is O(k) for the active unfinished token plus up to two pending backticks, excluding output retained by the caller.
- One pass preserves token order without sorting or backtracking. With callback emission, parser memory follows the largest unfinished token; bound it with a size or fragment policy.
solutionGuide: The base solution joins the chunks, making every split delimiter contiguous, then scans once with a mode and character-list buffer. It preserves stream order but doesn't emit incrementally. Triple backticks have priority in every mode; in fenced code, shorter runs are literal content. Empty buffers never produce a token.
